courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Academic Internship
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning. Must be integrated with an academic discipline. A written contract involving all parties will include learning objectives, a paper/project outline, and means of supervision and progress evaluation. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, and a completed and approved Learning Agreement for Special Studies.

courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Academic Internship Program
courses.description: Individual internship placements integrated with an academic discipline. A written contract involving all parties will include learning objectives, a paper/project outline, and means of supervision and progress evaluation. Consent of faculty adviser and program chair required. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of sixteen units.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; department approval.

courses.subject: AIP
courses.title: Public Service Internship
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning performed in nonprofit organizations or government agencies dedicated to providing services in the areas of education, government, social issues, and health. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of twelve units. Contract completed prior to start of internship will include intellectually unified expectations and means of supervision. Faculty member and student will meet regularly.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA; department approval.

courses.subject: AAS
courses.title: Independent Study in African American Studies
courses.description: Individual research and study on a particular subject related to African American studies by special arrangement with and under the direction of a faculty member. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Enrollment via the faculty director of the Black Diaspora and African American Studies program only.

courses.subject: ANAR
courses.title: Ancient Mediterranean Civilization
courses.description: Study Abroad Program that examines the origins and history of ancient Mediterranean civilizations from the late Neolithic period through the classical era. During the course, students will visit some of the most important archaeological sites in the world, from the ancient megalithic temples of Malta, to Phoenician colonies of the early Iron Age, to the Carthaginian and Greek cities of Sicily, and ending with Roman Pompeii and Herculaneum, destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79. Students are required to apply for this Study Abroad course. Program or materials fees may apply. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Department approval required.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Field Studies
courses.description: The Department of Anthropology has partnered with the Academic Internship Program (AIP) at UC San Diego to provide students with internship opportunities during their undergraduate studies. The AIP allows students to integrate academic theory and “real world” practice, engage in research that explores the relationship between the two, and gain hands-on experience in a professional setting. By participating, students receive ANTH 197 (P/NP) credit while fulfilling the requirements of the Academic Internship Program Office . In order to pursue this internship, you will need to have a faculty mentor from the anthropology department. Students will be responsible to follow the requirements outlined in the AIP syllabus, as well as plans established with the faculty mentor.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. Department approval required. Upper division standing required. May be taken for credit up to three times.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular department curriculum. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a UC San Diego GPA of at least 3.0 and consent of a bioengineering faculty member; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Industrial Internship
courses.description: Under the joint supervision of a faculty adviser and industry mentor, the student will work at or be mentored at a bioengineering industrial company to gain practical bioengineering experience, summarized in a technical report. May be taken for credit up to three times. With department approval, four units of credit may substitute for a technical elective. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of department and completion of all lower-division course requirements, including general-science requirement; laboratory experience. (F,W,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study, on a topic or in a field not included in the regular department curriculum, by arrangement with a bioengineering faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research by arrangement with a bioengineering faculty member. May be taken for credit three times. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form. (F,W,S,Su)

courses.subject: BENG
courses.title: Bioengineering Design Project and Industrial Training
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students focused on design, applied research, and professional experience.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department approval. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: BISP
courses.title: Biology Education Research
courses.description: Individual research on a problem in biology education by special arrangement with and under the direction of a faculty member. Projects are expected to involve novel research that examines issues in biology education such as the science of learning, evidence of effective teaching, and equity and inclusion in the classroom. P/PN grades only. May be taken for credit five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required. Enrollment is via department approval only. Students must complete a Special Studies form as well as a research plan. Paperwork for a BISP 193 must be submitted to SIS by all published deadlines as listed on the biology web page.

courses.subject: BISP
courses.title: Biology Internship Program
courses.description: Individual research on a problem by special arrangement with, and under the direction of, a UC San Diego faculty member and a selected researcher in industry or at a research institution. Projects are expected to involve primary, experimental/analytical approaches that augment training in basic biology and that echo the curricular focus of the School of Biological Sciences. Application deadlines are strictly enforced. Consult the School of Biological Sciences website for deadlines. Students must comply with all risk management policies/procedures. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required. Students must complete at least ninety units of credit and have a minimum GPA of 2.5. A completed and approved application/research plan/learning agreement is required for enrollment.

courses.subject: BISP
courses.title: Individual Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual research on a problem by special arrangement with, and under the direction of, a faculty member. Projects are expected to involve primary, experimental/analytical approaches that augment training in basic biology and that echo the curricular focus of the School of Biological Sciences. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit five times. Note: Students must apply to the school via the online system. For complete details, applications, and deadlines, please consult the School of Biological Sciences website. Application deadlines are strictly enforced.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required. Students must complete at least ninety units of credit and have a minimum GPA of 2.5.

courses.subject: CENG
courses.title: Introductory Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Kinematics and equation of motion; hydrostatics; Bernoulli’s equation; viscous flows; turbulence, pipe flow; boundary layers and drag in external flows; applications to chemical, structural, and bioengineering. Students may not receive credit for both MAE 101A and CENG 101A.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the major and grades of C– or better in PHYS 2A, MATH 20D, and MATH 20E, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CENG
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Research project as equivalent to a “senior thesis” can be approved for two technical elective courses (eight units total). This course is taken as an elective on a P/NP basis. It must be done in consecutive quarters and the student must find a faculty member who will oversee the research project. Eligible students must have completed at least ninety units and must have a UC San Diego cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better. Detailed policy and procedures may be obtained from the Student Affairs Office.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemistry Internship
courses.description: An internship program that provides work experience with public/private sector employers. Subject to the availability of positions, students will work in a local company under the supervision of a faculty member and site supervisor. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit a maximum of three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of ninety units with a minimum GPA of 2.5, and an approved Special Studies online application, and AIP learning agreement.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Reading and Research
courses.description: Independent literature or laboratory research by arrangement with, and under the direction of, a member of the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry faculty. Students must register on a P/NP basis.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, minimum GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor and department, and an approved Special Studies online application.

courses.subject: CLRE
courses.title: Patient-Oriented Research I
courses.description: This course will develop and apply the theory of clinical trials design and analysis, discuss the practical issues of financing and implementing clinical trials, and describe issues of monitoring trials and working in cooperative groups. The scholar will design and present a prospective clinical study protocol and participate in peer review of their colleagues’ work.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MAS in Clinical Research Program or consent of department.

courses.subject: CLRE
courses.title: Health Services Research
courses.description: Scholars will evaluate relevant outcomes in patient-oriented research from the patient (quality of life) and societal (economic) perspectives and locate potential resources for assessing the relevant outcomes in a wide variety of study designs. They will also be able to describe the relative strengths of different health services research approaches to a clinical problem. Finally, they will understand the components of clinical practice guidelines, including patient preferences, and how these guidelines both depend upon as well as inform patient-oriented research. Class sessions may also be offered live via distance learning with established remote site.

courses.subject: CLRE
courses.title: Biostatistics I
courses.description: The course will introduce the fundamentals of biostatistics and basic methods for analysis of continuous and binary outcomes for one, two, or several groups. Hands-on data analysis using the R statistical software and clinical research applications.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MAS Clinical Research Program or consent of department.

courses.subject: CLRE
courses.title: Directed Studies in Clinical Research
courses.description: Faculty member will direct a student’s study in selected professional development topics in clinical research. Specific content will be tailored to the student’s particular needs and interests. Students must make arrangements with the program and individual faculty member prior to enrolling in the course.
courses.prerequisites_text: MAS program or permission of department.

courses.subject: CLRE
courses.title: Independent Study Project
courses.description: Students conduct a high-level clinical research project that integrates what they have learned in their formal course work. The ISP will include their course work in CLRE 295A-B and be presented as a final report that includes a complete description of the project including the study manual, study results, statistical analysis, and a discussion of the findings. Students will make an oral presentation of their ISP to their three-member ISP committee comprised of faculty and industry advisers. The ISP is an independent, creative, and scholarly activity, and students will be graded on their written and oral presentations.
courses.prerequisites_text: CLRE 295A and admission to the MAS Clinical Research Program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: COGS
courses.title: Cognitive Science Internship
courses.description: The student will undertake a program of practical research in a supervised work environment. Topics to be researched may vary, but in each case the course will provide skills for carrying out these studies. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; 2.5 GPA; department approval.

courses.subject: COGS
courses.title: Special Project
courses.description: This independent study course is for individual, advanced students who wish to complete a one-quarter reading or research project under the mentorship of a faculty member. Students should contact faculty whose research interests them to discuss possible projects. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; 2.5 GPA; consent of instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: COGS
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Students study and research selected topics under the direction of a member of the faculty.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Introduction to Computational Social Science
courses.description: Overview of causal and statistical inference, data types/structure, and modeling/analytical approaches to social science data. Topics include models of social phenomena at different scales (cognition, behavior, learning, communication, language, game theory, markets, etc.) and analysis of different types of social data (social networks, text, GIS, timeseries, etc.). Emphasis is placed on the understanding of analytical and modeling methods, their applications and limitations. Open to CT75 majors only.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Computational Social Science Technical Boot Camp
courses.description: This course provides practical experience with the technical skills underpinning computational social science. Topics may include calculus, linear algebra, probability, Unix/Linux, working in the terminal, file encoding, file system organization, Python, numpy, pandas, scikit, notebooks, matplotlib, code style, scraping, data storage, SQL, JSON, CSV/TSV, version control, git, spreadsheets, algorithms, basic data visualization, and machine learning basics. Open to CT75 majors only.

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Seminar in CSE
courses.description: A seminar course on topics of current interest. Students, as well as the instructor, will be actively involved in running the course/class. This course cannot be counted toward a technical elective.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Field Study in Computer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Directed study accompanying full-time on-site computer science internships. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor and approval of the department required. Students may receive credit for one of the following: CSE 197 or CSE 197C. Restricted to CS25, CS26, CS27, and CS29 majors only.

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Special Project in Computer Science and Engineering
courses.description: The student will conceive, design, and execute a project in computer science under the direction of a faculty member. The project will typically include a large programming or hardware design task, but other types of projects are possible.
courses.prerequisites_text: CSE graduate student status. (CS 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81) (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to properly qualified graduate students who wish to pursue a problem through advanced study under the direction of a member of the staff. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CSE
courses.title: Research
courses.description: Research.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of faculty.

courses.subject: CGS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Tutorial; independent study on a topic not generally included in the curriculum.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and director of Critical Gender Studies Program and department stamp required.

courses.subject: CAT
courses.title: Sixth College Practicum Global Seminar
courses.description: This course will have students initiate, plan, and carry out research-based and/or community-based projects. These projects will connect classroom-based experiences and knowledge to the outlying community, and explicitly explore the interplay of culture, art, and technology. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; department authorization required.

courses.subject: CAT
courses.title: Public Rhetoric and Practical Communication Global Seminar
courses.description: Upper-division composition course in public rhetoric and practical communication, including oral presentation, writing in print formats, and digital content-creation. This course also focuses on how writing can support and extend experiential learning before, during, or after students complete their experiential learning requirement. Completion of lower-division writing requirement is preferred but not required. It is recommended that students pursuing graduate degrees select “Letter Grade” at the time of enrollment. This course is a distance education course. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; department authorization required.

courses.subject: DSC
courses.title: Data Science Internship
courses.description: Individual research on a topic related to data science, by special arrangement with and under the direction of a faculty member, in connection with an internship at an organization. Internship work will inform but not necessarily define the research topic. The research topic is expected to promote the study of the principles and techniques involved in the internship work. Students should independently secure an internship before enrolling in the course.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to students with upper-division standing. Consent of the instructor and approval of the department. An application for Special Studies must be filed with the Registrar’s office after approval from the instructor and the department chair.

courses.subject: DSC
courses.title: Independent Study for Data Science Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a topic related to data science by special arrangement with a faculty member. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to students with upper-division standing. Consent of the instructor and approval of the department. An application for Special Studies must be filed with the Registrar’s Office after approval from the instructor and the department chair.

courses.subject: DSC
courses.title: DSC Graduate Internship
courses.description: Internship with institution or agency allowing students to pursue topics raised in the data science core and/or elective courses. May be taken for credit up to four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Restricted to DS75 and DS76 students.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Cognitive Development and Education
courses.description: This course examines the development of cognition, thinking, and language from infancy to adolescence with implications for education. Topics include learning theories, executive function, memory and language, as well as impacts of technology, poverty, diversity, and bilingualism. Course content focuses on addressing achievement gaps. Students may not receive credit for both EDS 115 and EDS 115GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division or graduate majors ED 78 or ED 76 standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Language, Culture, and Education
courses.description: (Same as SOCI 117) Representations of language and culture will be explored in education; explanations of students’ school successes and challenges drawing on sociocultural and linguistic factors will be considered; bilingualism, cultural transmission, and identity development through education. Students may not receive credit for EDS 117 and SOCI 117 and EDS 117GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: History, Politics, and Theory of Bilingual Education
courses.description: This course provides a historical overview and models of bilingual education in the United States. Students will examine sociocultural, theoretical, and policy issues associated with native language and second-language instruction, and legal requirements for public bilingual program.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Practicum in Teaching and Learning
courses.description: Students are placed in local P–12 schools and community field sites to actively engage in face-to-face educational service work. Students spend a minimum of four hours per week consistently over the ten-week quarter for a minimum total of forty hours per quarter. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit up to twelve times. Corequisites: One of the following courses must be taken concurrently: EDS 128A-B, or 129A-B-C, 130, 131, 133, 136, 137, 140, 141, 145, or 146.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Special Studies
courses.description: Individual guided reading and study involving research and analysis of activities and services in multicultural education, bilingual education, the teaching-learning process, and other areas that are not covered by the present curriculum.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Introduction to Resources for Teaching and Learning
courses.description: This course introduces students to educational resources, both in print and online. Students compile and evaluate research studies, curricular materials, and instructional approaches in preparation for future projects in developing and evaluating various approaches to teaching and learning.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must be registered EDS graduate students (ED 76, 77, 78, 79, 80).

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Technology, Teaching, and Learning
courses.description: This course will review current literature on effective applications of technology in the classroom. Students will also become fluent in the use of productivity tools, presentation software, and web development for teaching and learning; critique software relevant to their area of teaching; and develop an educational activity based on their review of the literature that harnesses the power of technology.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must be registered EDS graduate students (ED 76, 77, 78, 79, 80).

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Technology and Professional Assessment
courses.description: Advanced techniques for using network-based resources for teaching and learning will be introduced. Students will review relevant research on advanced technologies related to assessment of professional performance and student achievement. Students will present a web-based professional Teaching Performance Assessment Portfolio that reflects teaching performance during their student teaching or internship field experience. This course is a distance education course. Students will not receive credit for both EDS 204 and EDS 204R.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must be registered as an MEd/Credential graduate student (ED78).

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Teaching Performance Assessment Portfolio
courses.description: This course introduces the use of a Teaching Performance Assessment Portfolio for assessment of teaching performance. Student teachers and interns will design an electronic portfolio that demonstrates acceptable performance on essential credential standards. National Board of Professional Teaching Standards will also be introduced. This course is a distance education course. Students will not receive credit for both EDS 206R and EDS 206.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must be registered EDS graduate students.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Equitable Educational Research and Practice
courses.description: This course introduces students to research studies and educational practices of educational equity, both in general and within specific content areas. Research studies relevant to educational equity will be examined, as will practices that have attempted to enable all students to achieve to the best of their abilities.
courses.prerequisites_text: students must be registered EDS graduate students.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Leadership for Learning
courses.description: This course will explore various models of curriculum and instruction in response to students’ learning needs. It also will examine models of school organization and the leader’s role and responsibility in developing a school culture that promotes student achievement, using evidence-based decision making. A major emphasis will be on evaluating research on which theories and practice are based.
courses.prerequisites_text: Joint EdD in Educational Leadership student status (ED81).

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Leadership for Organizational Development
courses.description: This course will investigate the skills and dispositions needed for students to lead the development of learning organizations. Faculty will teach and model concepts of working with people within educational organizations and programs. Emphasis will be placed on individual’s team development and facilitation, organizational communications, adult learning, and professional development.
courses.prerequisites_text: Joint EdD in Educational Leadership student status or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Leadership
courses.description: This course explores topical issues in the field of leadership. It focuses on recent developments that have broad implications for research and practice in educational leadership. Course topics will vary each time the course is offered.
courses.prerequisites_text: Joint EdD in Educational Leadership student status.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Dissertation Writing Seminar
courses.description: This seminar provides an opportunity for doctoral candidates to present and critique in-progress dissertation research and writing. Topics addressed will also include writing for professional publications and presenting research findings to varied audiences. This is the third in a four-course series.
courses.prerequisites_text: EDS 289B, and Joint EdD in Educational Leadership student status or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Supervised research studies with individual topics selected according to students’ special interests. Students will develop a research proposal appropriate for MA thesis, begin to gather and analyze data.
courses.prerequisites_text: MA candidate and consent of instructor. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic for students who have been admitted to candidacy for the EdD or PhD program. May be taken for credit up to four times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission into the EdD or PhD program (major codes ED81 and ED82) and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Secondary English Teaching Practices
courses.description: The course introduces prospective secondary teachers to principles and strategies of teaching English language arts. Topics include writing processes, reading processes, integrated language arts, assessment, the second language learner, the classroom community, the California English Language Arts Framework.
courses.prerequisites_text: ED78 Single Subject major only. Affirmed Single Subject candidate at UC San Diego who has advanced to internship or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Secondary Mathematics Teaching Practices
courses.description: Mathematics teaching techniques, including curriculum design, California Model Curriculum Standards, instructional methods, computer applications, selection and use of textbooks, student assessment, lesson planning, and classroom organization. Professional matters including curriculum planning, professional organizations, para-professionals, professional ethics, education law, and parent involvement are addressed.
courses.prerequisites_text: ED78 Single Subject major only. Affirmed Single Subject candidate at UC San Diego who has advanced to internship or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Secondary Science Teaching Practices
courses.description: Science teaching techniques, including science curriculum design, California Model Curriculum Standards, instructional methods, computer applications, selection and use of textbooks, student assessment, lesson planning, and classroom organization. Professional matters including curriculum planning, professional organizations, paraprofessionals, professional ethics, education law, and parent involvement are addressed.
courses.prerequisites_text: ED78 Single Subject major only. Affirmed Single Subject candidate at UC San Diego who has advanced to internship or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDS
courses.title: Language and Learning Instruction
courses.description: This course satisfies the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing requirement for preparation in reading theory and methods for all credential candidates. Theories of reading development, integration of the language arts, reading and writing in the content areas, teaching methods, and literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: ED78 Elementary Multiple Subject or Single Subject candidates at UC San Diego who have advanced to student teaching or internship.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Advanced Digital Design Project
courses.description: Advanced topics in digital circuits and systems. Use of computers and design automation tools. Hazard elimination, synchronous/asynchronous FSM synthesis, synchronization and arbitration, pipelining and timing issues. Problem sets and design exercises. A large-scale design project. Simulation and/or rapid prototyping.
courses.prerequisites_text: ECE 25 or CSE 140.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: ECE Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program that provides work experience with public/private section employers. Subject to the availability of positions, students will work in a local company under the supervision of a faculty member and site supervisor. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: minimum UC San Diego 2.5 GPA. Consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Open to properly qualified graduate students who wish to pursue a problem through advanced study under the direction of a member of the staff. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Research
courses.description: (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: LTEN
courses.title: Special Studies
courses.description: Tutorial; individual guided reading in an area not normally covered in courses. May be taken for credit up to four times. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Prehistory and Ancient Foundations
courses.description: MMW 11R is a distance education course. This course explores human origins, the development of early forms of social and political organization, the strategies that early societies used to negotiate their physical and social environments, and the appearance of influential cultural traditions across the ancient world (to circa 100 BCE). Topics include the emergence of agriculture, the relationship between nomad and settled, the birth of the city and the expanding human “footprint,” the development of writing, foundational religious and cosmological ideas and narratives, influential models of visual and material culture, and changing forms of social stratification and inequality. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 11 and MMW 11R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Transforming Traditions and Emerging World Communities, circa 100 BCE–1200 CE
courses.description: MMW 12R is a distance education course. This course provides a global perspective on the past from circa 100 BCE to circa 1200 CE, examining the emergence of interregional networks and empires and their relationship with the advent and expansion of diverse religious movements, including Christianity, Islam, and Buddhism, as well as cross-cultural contacts and exchanges. The course also explores forms of identity (ethnic, religious, and other); models of inclusion and exclusion; systems of power, hierarchy, and slavery; and the human-environmental relationship. MMW 12 is the first of two writing-intensive courses in the MMW sequence. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 12 and MMW 12R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: A Globalizing World: Exchanges, Entanglements, and Exploitation, Thirteenth–Eighteenth Century
courses.description: MMW 13R is a distance education course. This course presents a global perspective on the connections, exchanges, and transformations that linked Afro-Eurasia and the Americas during the period from 1200 to 1750 CE. The course examines the nature and consequences of this increasingly connected world. It focuses on spaces of cross-cultural contact and exchange, including the transfer of technologies, ideas, commodities, and customs and their environmental impact; encounters in the form of travel, trade, migration, and invasion; and exploitation through empire, colonization, and slavery, and their manifestation in state violence, intolerance, discrimination, and racism. MMW 13 is the second of two writing-intensive courses in the MMW sequence. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 13 and MMW 13R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Divergent Paths to the Modern World, Eighteenth–Twentieth Century
courses.description: MMW 14R is a distance education course. This course explores divergent paths to modernity between the mid-eighteenth century and World War I. The course examines the influence of “the West” as a hegemonic force that disrupted global connections and forged new ones, changing the social, economic, political, and ecological norms of societies worldwide. The course investigates how groups and individuals around the world adopted, contested, and/or resisted this influence. Students may receive credit for MMW 14 with any one of the following: MMW 14, MMW 14R, or MMW 14GS. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R and MMW 13 or MMW 13R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: The Contemporary Era: Conflict and Aspirations in a Globalized World, Twentieth–Twenty-First Century
courses.description: This course explores the sociocultural, economic, and political forces that shaped the twentieth and twenty-first century and contestations over them, with particular focus on the complex interaction between humans and the natural world. It examines the overlapping causes and impact of the global and local conflicts and inequalities that have defined the contemporary era. The course addresses efforts to defend and expand freedom, improve quality of life, and increase transnational cooperation and communication that challenge those hierarchies that perpetuate inequality. The course reflects on what this recent history may mean for our collective future. Students may receive credit for MMW 15 with any one of the following: MMW 15, MMW 15R, or MMW 15GS. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement. Satisfies the Jane Teranes Climate Change Education Requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R and MMW 13 or MMW 13R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: The Contemporary Era: Conflict and Aspirations in a Globalized World, Twentieth–Twenty-First Century
courses.description: MMW 15R is a distance education course. This course explores the sociocultural, economic, and political forces that shaped the twentieth and twenty-first century and contestations over them, with particular focus on the complex interaction between humans and the natural world. It examines the overlapping causes and impact of the global and local conflicts and inequalities that have defined the contemporary era. The course addresses efforts to defend and expand freedom, improve quality of life, and increase transnational cooperation and communication that challenge those hierarchies that perpetuate inequality. The course reflects on what this recent history may mean for our collective future. Students may receive credit for MMW 15 with any one of the following: MMW 15, MMW 15R, or MMW 15GS. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement. Satisfies the Jane Teranes Climate Change Education Requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R and MMW 13 or MMW 13R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Exploring the Premodern World
courses.description: MMW 121R is a distance education course. This course addresses themes and topics from the premodern world (from antiquity to the eighteenth century), and strengthens students’ analytical, research, and writing skills. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 121 and MMW 121R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) transfer students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Exploring the Modern World
courses.description: MMW 122R is a distance education course. This course addresses specific themes and topics from the modern world (from the eighteenth century to the present), and strengthens transfer students’ analytical, research, and writing skills. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 122 and MMW 122R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) transfer students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Subject to the approval of a faculty adviser, students may choose courses offered by departments participating in the Materials Science and Engineering Program. Please see the graduate coordinator for more information.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Extracurricular Industry Practicum
courses.description: An enrichment program which provides academic credit for work experience with public/private sector employers. After independently securing an internship with significant mathematical content, students will identify a faculty member to work with directly, discussing the mathematics involved. Faculty may require related readings and assignments as appropriate. May be taken for credit three times. Units may not be applied towards major graduation requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: permission of department.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading in advanced mathematics by individual students. Three periods. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: permission of department.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics Graduate Research Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program that provides work experience with public/private sector employers and researchers. Under supervision of a faculty adviser, students provide mathematical consultation services. May be taken up to three times for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Reading and Research
courses.description: Independent study and research for the doctoral dissertation. One to three credits will be given for independent study (reading) and one to nine for research.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Engineering Internship
courses.description: Students work in local industry or hospitals under faculty supervision. Units may not be applied toward graduation requirements. Salaried or unsalaried. Number of units determined by enrollment frequency. First quarter up to four units. Subsequent quarters cannot exceed one unit.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department stamp, 2.50 overall GPA minimum, at least ninety units.

courses.subject: MAE
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing theses. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Online version of the first course of sequence in university reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students who have not completed a comparable course elsewhere. MCWP 40R introduces students to the basic elements of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. This class is held synchronously online. Grades of C or higher are required for prerequisites. Must take MCWP 40R for a letter grade for the Muir College writing requirement. Credit given for only one of the following: MCWP 40, MCWP 40R, MCWP 40C, or MCWP 40CR. This is a distance education course.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Online version of the second course of sequence in reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students. MCWP 50R focuses on advanced skills of argument and analyses. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. This class is held synchronously online. Students will not receive credit for both MCWP 50 and MCWP 50R. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy the Muir College writing requirement. This is a distance education course.

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and departmental chair.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thesis Research in Physics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or laboratory research under direction of faculty in the Department of Psychology. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: MPH Practicum Field Placement
courses.description: This course provides MPH students the opportunity to participate in a short-term, field-based public health or population-based experience. Students will engage in a field experience in collaboration with a sponsoring organization and qualified site mentor. Students are expected to apply theory, skills, and training acquired through the public health course work within a real-life setting. Students will develop written and oral communication skills that employ public health concepts and methods.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Renumbered from FMPH 496B. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 496B and PH 496B.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Independent study for biostatistics graduate students in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science. Study of special topics for graduate students under the direction of a faculty member. Exact subject matter to be arranged in individual cases. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors. May be taken for credit up to twenty-one times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Capstone: Applied Finance Project
courses.description: The Capstone project is one of the primary measures of student learning. Evaluation is based on students’ ability to apply course material to the Capstone project. Satisfactory completion of the project is required for award of the degree. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTF 402, MGTF 403, MGTF 404, and restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Directed individual study or research by special arrangement and under supervision of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department approval; approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Leading People
courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, introduces principles of effective teamwork and leadership and of strategic managerial communication. Provides an introduction to case study and to ethical issues confronting managers in technology or science-driven firms. Develops managerial communication skills. Letter grades only. Students will not earn credit for both MGT 406 and MGT 406R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or department or instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Current Business Law Issues
courses.description: Explores current issues in business law, emphasizing concerns faced by new companies. Students learn how the law regulates and shapes businesses; examine the legal role in business formations, operations, and dissolutions; and gain knowledge of contract and intellectual property law. Letter grades only. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 417 and MGT 212. Also, students may not receive credit for both MGT 417 and MGT 219 with the course subtitle Current Business Law Issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA students only or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: CEO, the Board of Directors, and Corporate Governance
courses.description: Provides an understanding of relationships among shareholders, managers, and boards. Focuses on the office of the chief executive officer and on the board of directors, including the roles and responsibilities of directors, and the legal, economic, managerial, and psychological issues they confront. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 421 and MGT 211. They are course equivalents.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Biotechnology Industry, Structure, and Strategy
courses.description: Provides a business overview of the life science industry, its major market segments, financial structure, and financing strategies. Develops an understanding of major industry issues and strategies, including business development, financing, partnering and alliances, emerging trends, ethical and policy issues. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 430 and MGT 250. They are course equivalents.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in management and organizational behavior. Instructional methods include face-to-face lecture, case presentations, assigned readings, and online group discussions. May be taken for credit four times, for a maximum of sixteen units if the topics are significantly different. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 439 and MGT 269 when they have the same subtitles.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in International Business
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in international business. Instructional methods include face-to-face lecture, case presentations, assigned readings, and group discussions. May be taken for credit four times, for a maximum of sixteen units if the topics are significantly different. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 443 and MGT 229 when the course subtitles are the same.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Describes the systems approach to managing the entire flow of information, materials, and services from raw materials suppliers through factories and warehouses to the end customer, which is the key to productivity and competitiveness of manufacturing and service enterprises. The course integrates issues from marketing (channels of distribution), logistics, and operations. No credit for MGT 453 if taken after MGT 453R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Brand Management
courses.description: A brand is a company’s most important asset, driving financial success, loyalty, and competitive advantage. This course takes a strong stance on brand management, viewing brands as cocreations of consumers and marketers. Brand managers navigate meaning-making, ensuring resonance, value, and risk mitigation over time. Using case studies, the course emphasizes real-world applications, fostering collaborative discussions that enhance learning beyond any single instructor’s expertise. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 482 and MGT 482R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or by instructor or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Brand Management
courses.description: A brand is a company’s most important asset, driving financial success, loyalty, and competitive advantage. This course takes a strong stance on brand management, viewing brands as cocreations of consumers and marketers. Brand managers navigate meaning-making, ensuring resonance, value, and risk mitigation over time. Using case studies the course emphasizes real-world applications, fostering collaborative discussions that enhance learning beyond any single instructor’s expertise. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 482R and MGT 482. This is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or by instructor or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Finance
courses.description: Advanced topics in finance. Instructional methods include face-to-face lecture and case discussion. May be taken for credit four times, for a maximum of sixteen units if the topics are significantly different. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 495 and MGT 282 when the course subtitles are the same.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Advanced Management Research Practicum
courses.description: Internship with approved business or governmental agency, allowing student to pursue topics raised in the management core and elective courses. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit four times, for a maximum of four units, with instructor consent. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 497 and MGT 297. Internship credit may not be applied to fulfill specific course requirements or to credits required for graduation.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Individual Directed Study
courses.description: Individual study or research under the direction of a selected faculty member. May be taken for credit twelve times. Students may earn credit for a total of twelve units in MGT 299 and/or MGT 499.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: AI-Assisted Math and Programming for Business Analytics
courses.description: Success in business analytics (aka data science for business) requires a solid foundation in mathematics, statistics, and programming. This course is designed to enhance students’ ability to solve math and programming challenges using AI tools like ChatGPT (Code Interpreter) and GitHub Co-Pilot X. This AI-assisted course will be the start of the students’ learning journey and will set students up to create analytical solutions to important business problems.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MS in business analytics students or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Business Analytics in Marketing, Finance, and Operations
courses.description: Business analytics projects should strive to create substantial value to an organization by solving impactful business problems. In this class, students will learn to identify business opportunities in the substantive areas of marketing, finance, and operations. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: SQL and ETL
courses.description: Most organizations store transaction data (e.g., sales, purchases, production, etc.) in relational databases. These databases are of central importance in most business analytics projects. To access and analyze this data, knowledge of SQL (structured query language), one of the most sought-after skills by recruiters, is needed. In this course, students will learn how to write SQL statements to extract and transform data. Students will be introduced to ETL (extract, transform, and load) concepts.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MS in business analytics students.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Independent Research Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent research in religion under the supervision of a faculty member affiliated with the Program for the Study of Religion. This course may be repeated three times with program approval. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, with 2.5 GPA (overall); program stamp.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Climate Math and Science
courses.description: The course will introduce key physical and biogeochemical concepts needed to understand the Earth’s climate system. The overview will provide a foundation for examining the physical evidence of climate change. Mathematical methods will be presented to reinforce the scientific concepts. Students will complete group papers and presentations and lead discussions on assigned readings. SIOC 290S is a required course in the curriculum of the master of advanced studies—climate science and policy. (Letter grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Introduction to Climate Policy
courses.description: The course will focus on policy solutions to climate change and introduce key topics in state, national, and international environmental law and policy. The energy system as well as energy policy will be examined, providing essential foundation for understanding California’s renewable energy policy goals and how we may get there. Students will complete group papers and presentations and lead discussions on assigned readings. This course will include a one-week field trip (Letter grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Marine Biodiversity and Conservation—Lab
courses.description: Laboratory work on major biological taxa, field trips on biodiversity in situ, computer labs for informatic tools. Students are expected to attend field trips at sea and to various sites around San Diego County as part of the course. Students get practical experience in fieldwork, public speaking, visual communication, and team building. Students who have taken SIO 295L may not receive credit for SIO 295LS. Corequisites: SIO 295S.
courses.prerequisites_text: MAS MBC students only; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Marine Biodiversity and Conservation—Seminar
courses.description: Lectures on biology, ecology, economics, social issues, policies, and governance of marine biodiversity. Includes global case studies on ecology and socioeconomic and governance issues, with strong emphasis on practicing written, verbal, and visual communication skills and collaborative group work. Students are expected to attend field trips at sea and to various sites around San Diego County as part of the corequisite course. Students who have taken SIO 295 may not receive credit for SIO 295S. Corequisites: SIO 295LS.
courses.prerequisites_text: MAS MBC students only; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Language, Culture, and Education
courses.description: (Same as EDS 117.) The mutual influence of language, culture, and education will be explored; explanations of students’ school successes and failures that employ linguistic and cultural variables will be considered; bilingualism; cultural transmission through education.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 117 and SOCB 117.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Tutorial: individual study under the direction of an interested faculty member in an area not covered by the present course offerings. Approval must be secured from the departmental committee on independent studies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval required.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Engineering Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program, available to a limited number of undergraduate students, which provides work experience with industry, government offices, etc., under the supervision of a faculty member and industrial supervisor. Coordination of the Engineering Internship is conducted through UC San Diego’s Academic Internship Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of ninety units with a 2.5 GPA and consent of department chair. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: WES
courses.title: Software for Embedded Systems
courses.description: Embedded computing elements, device interfaces, time-critical I/O handling. Embedded software design under size, performance, and reliability constraints. Software timing and functional validation. Programming methods and compilation for embeddable software. Embedded runtime systems. Case studies of real-time software systems.
